report.summary: Reviewed chunk 3 of 7 of embeddings.py, lines 561-700. Enumerated public symbols and checkable claims.
risks: _record_identity_anchor | medium | Docstring claims anchor costs no extra embedding call and checks invariant; code shows it selects first projection by created_at, but does not verify embedding consistency here. What would settle it: check if embedding comparison is done elsewhere after anchor is set.

claims.why: The docstring claims possible return values, but the code only returns 'missing' or row['provenance']. The values 'created' or 'adopted' are not defined in this chunk; they depend on caller or other parts.

claims.text: Re-using a real projection rather than a synthetic probe text means the anchor costs no extra embedding call at index-creation time
claims.why: The function selects an existing projection from event_projections; it does not call any embedding backend.

claims.text: checks precisely the invariant that matters: the vectors already in this index are still what this backend produces.
claims.why: The code only selects a candidate and inserts an anchor row. No verification of embedding consistency is performed in this chunk; the claim refers to a check that must occur elsewhere.

observations.what: Schema creation includes multiple tables and indexes, plus a view conditional on absence of agent_events table.
_resolved_spec validates multiple fields against requested spec, raising ValueError on mismatch.
_ensure_index inserts row then fetches and compares full spec; raises RuntimeError on failure or mismatch.
_record_identity_anchor silently returns if anchor already exists or if no candidate projection found.
